program_note:
Possible Worlds is a set of three short “studies” for solo cello, written between 1989 and 1991. The first, Intonazione, explores and tests the cellist’s intonation and, through its slow expansion of sonorities, acts as a warm-up to the next two pieces. Possible Worlds, the second movement, is an exploration of different pizzicato and glissando effects. The last movement, Doubles for a Minute?, is so named because most every note is repeated (doubled), most every note is a double stop, and the entire movement should take exactly a minute to play. In line with the title of the third movement, an alternate title for the entire work could be “Cello, Anyone?”.  Possible Worlds and Doubles for a Minute? may each be performed individually. The first movement though, Intonazione, should not be performed independently of the other two movements. The duration of the entire work is between six and seven minutes, with the first two movements between 2.5 and 3 minutes and the last movement (ideally!) exactly one minute.

Possible Worlds was begun in late Fall, 1989, as a one-movement solo cello work. The piece was written for, and was dedicated to, Wilhelmina Smith, who premièred it in January, 1990. The first movement of this three-movement version was begun in early 1991, and was intended as a graduation present for Mina Smith. I did not complete it, however, until October, 1991, with the help of James Holland. That movement, and the work as a whole, is dedicated to both of them. I began and completed the last movement in October, 1991, again with the invaluable help of James Holland, who premièred the entire work in February, 1992. That last movement is dedicated to him.

David S. Lefkowitz

29 February, 1992

Rochester, New York
